extracted.intended_audience: Banks subject to U.S. federal supervision (compliance officers, AML/CFT program managers), bank senior management and boards, outside auditors/consultants, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory requirements and supervisory expectations for banks' AML/CFT programs—including risk assessments, CDD, independent testing, officer designation, training, written program approval/access, supervision/enforcement, and information-sharing with FinCEN. Intended to guide banks on how to establish, maintain, and demonstrate an effective, risk-based AML/CFT program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of AML/CFT Priorities into risk assessment processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must incorporate the AML/CFT Priorities in a bank's risk assessment processes, as appropriate; after reviewing the AML/CFT Priorities, a bank may determine the extent to which a particular Priority is applicable and whether and how it should be incorporated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Banks may use judgment and a reasonable, risk-based determination to focus on specific aspects of a Priority rather than all aspects. However, a surface-level, perfunctory review that fails to consider foreseeable ways a Priority may manifest in customers, products/services, geographies, and channels would not satisfy the requirement. Example: patterns consistent with potential structuring should not be dismissed without determining potential connections to other illicit finance activity. When AML/CFT Priorities are updated, banks need only incorporate the most recent Priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updates to risk assessment processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must update their risk assessment processes promptly upon any change that the bank would know or have reason to know would significantly change their ML/TF risk profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples triggering updates include new or significantly changed products/services/customer types, adoption of new risk-mitigation technology, mergers/acquisitions/divestitures, and external changes that significantly affect ML/TF risks. Agencies solicited comment on what 'promptly' means and whether alternatives (periodic updates or 'materially changes') would be preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-based allocation of attention and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: AML/CFT programs should be risk-based, directing more attention and resources toward higher-risk customers and activities consistent with the bank's risk profile, rather than toward lower-risk customers and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule adopts the formulation from Section 6101(b) of the AML Act. Banks are given flexibility to deploy resources without fear of supervisory criticism for focusing on higher-risk areas. The goal is to devote fewer resources to lower priority activities so banks can be more effective at detecting, reporting, and preventing illicit funds flows. Examiners will assess whether (1) resource allocation decisions are informed by and consistent with reasonably designed risk assessment processes; and (2) whether the bank knows or should know of resource-related issues that could result in failing to implement its AML/CFT program in all material respects and has failed to address such issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct ongoing customer due diligence (CDD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk-based procedures for conducting ongoing CDD—understanding the nature and purpose of customer relationships and conducting ongoing monitoring—are required as part of a bank's AML/CFT program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CDD activities include monitoring relationships, maintaining and updating customer information on a risk basis, and identifying and reporting suspicious transactions. CDD is incorporated within the requirement for a risk-based and reasonably designed set of internal policies, procedures, and controls (not as a standalone pillar). This alignment mirrors FinCEN's CDD component and reflects supervisory expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent testing of AML/CFT program
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must establish independent AML/CFT program testing to be conducted by bank personnel or an outside party; independent testing assesses compliance with AML/CFT statutory and regulatory requirements relative to the bank's risk profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent testing should focus on whether the AML/CFT program is effective and identify issues for remediation. Testing should be based on objective criteria assessing whether the program is established and implemented effectively and whether resources are allocated consistent with risk assessment processes; it should evaluate project governance and compensating controls. Testing must be independent of the function being tested; individuals who report (directly or indirectly) to the AML/CFT officer or who are involved in AML/CFT functions (e.g., training, policy development) generally would not be sufficiently independent. Outside parties conducting testing must not be government agencies/regulators. Less complex, lower-risk banks may use shared resources or internal staff not involved in the function being tested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of an AML/CFT officer responsible for program implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: A bank must designate an individual(s) (AML/CFT officer) responsible for establishing and implementing the AML/CFT program and coordinating and monitoring day-to-day compliance with the BSA and FinCEN regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AML/CFT officer must be qualified, not overburdened with other responsibilities, have decision-making capability, and sufficient functional stature within the organization to ensure compliance. The officer's authority, independence, and access to resources (compliance funds, staffing with appropriate skills, supportive organizational structure, and sufficient technology/systems) are critical. Conflicting responsibilities that impair the officer's ability to coordinate and monitor day-to-day compliance generally would not meet the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: AML/CFT officer must be located in the United States and accessible to regulators
rubrics_metrics.description: The person(s) performing the duty to establish, maintain, and enforce a bank's AML/CFT program must be persons in the United States who are accessible to, and subject to oversight and supervision by, the Secretary and the appropriate Federal functional regulator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While some AML/CFT functions may be performed by personnel outside the U.S. or by third-party providers abroad, the designated AML/CFT officer must be U.S.-located. The requirement aligns with FinCEN's interpretation; it does not alter other regulations restricting SAR sharing with non-U.S. personnel except in limited circumstances (e.g., foreign head office). Agencies requested comment on clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing employee training program
rubrics_metrics.description: AML/CFT programs must include an ongoing employee training program covering the bank's internal policies, procedures, and controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training content and frequency depend on the bank's ML/TF risk profile and the roles/responsibilities of trainees. Training should reflect risk assessment results, latest AML/CFT regulatory requirements, and other relevant information. The rule is risk-based and provides flexibility to identify employees and non-employees who must be trained on an ongoing basis. Agencies requested comment on clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written AML/CFT program availability upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must have a written AML/CFT program that must be made available upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is consistent with current Agency rules; the proposed rule would move and harmonize existing requirements and requests comment on whether further clarification is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of written AML/CFT program by board/equivalent or senior management
rubrics_metrics.description: A bank's written AML/CFT program must be approved by the bank's board of directors, an equivalent governing body, or appropriate senior management; approval must encompass each of the components of the AML/CFT program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent governing bodies could include a foreign banking organization's board for a U.S. branch, or a board committee (e.g., compliance committee). Senior management approvers may include CEO, CFO, COO, CLO, CCO, directors, or senior committees. Although board approval is no longer required in all cases, agencies still expect boards to provide appropriate oversight through other means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Identification Program (CIP) requirement maintained
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule maintains current Customer Identification Program requirements, moving them to a separate section and requiring a customer identification program be implemented as part of the AML/CFT program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes are technical and non-substantive, updating terminology to 'AML/CFT' and harmonizing language across Agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for supervision and enforcement terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule defines key terms such as 'AML/CFT requirement,' 'AML/CFT enforcement action,' and 'significant AML/CFT supervisory action' for use in the supervision and enforcement framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'AML/CFT requirement' covers BSA and related regulations; 'AML/CFT enforcement action' includes formal/informal agency actions (cease-and-desist, written/consent orders, MOU, civil money penalties); 'significant AML/CFT supervisory action' means written communications/formal supervisory determinations identifying deficiencies and contemplating significant or programmatic remedial measures (excluding informal examiner observations). Agencies are adding clarifying definitions into Subpart B as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement and supervision policy regarding program-established banks
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for a significant or systemic failure to implement in all material respects an established AML/CFT program, a bank that has properly established an AML/CFT program would not be subject to an AML/CFT enforcement action or significant AML/CFT supervisory action based on the program rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy applies to actions by the Agencies and is not intended to restrict actions relating to a failure to establish a program. The provision clarifies supervisory expectations aligned with the AML Act's emphasis on effectiveness and risk-based supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: FinCEN consultation and notice requirement before Agency enforcement/supervisory action
rubrics_metrics.description: Before initiating an AML/CFT enforcement action or significant supervisory action, an Agency would provide the Director of FinCEN written notice of intent at least 30 days in advance, unless a shorter period is necessary to remedy, prevent, or respond to an unsafe or unsound practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must be accompanied by relevant AML/CFT information underlying the proposed action (e.g., draft ROE portions, draft enforcement action portions, examination workpapers, or bank-submitted AML/CFT information). Agencies are not obligated to provide information over which the bank may claim privilege and will respond to reasonable requests for additional AML/CFT information from the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted information sharing with FinCEN Director and privilege preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks may share information with the FinCEN Director that relates to an existing or potential AML/CFT enforcement action or significant AML/CFT supervisory action, including information ordinarily considered non-public by the Agencies, provided the information has an appropriate nexus to the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two alternative approaches are proposed: Option 1—Agency authorizes disclosure of covered information to the FinCEN Director and permits the Director to use it (mirrors 12 U.S.C. 1821(t)); Option 2—Agency authorizes disclosure and Director's use but requires banks to contemporaneously disclose the same non-public information to the Agency (arguably better preserves privilege). Both options permit FinCEN Director to use but not further disclose the information; dissemination beyond the Director is governed by Agency disclosure rules. Additional text seeks to preserve applicable privileges and prevent unintended destruction of privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal policies, procedures, and controls must be risk-based and reasonably designed
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule requires that internal policies, procedures, and controls be 'risk-based' and 'reasonably designed' to ensure compliance with the BSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies request comment on whether banks expect changes to existing internal policies under this framing. The requirement ties internal controls to the bank's risk assessment processes and overall program effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple risk assessment processes and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule refers to 'risk assessment processes' (plural), allowing banks to use findings from one or more processes to assess ML/TF risk rather than prescribing a single, monolithic process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies solicit comment on whether this provides sufficient flexibility and how to better describe 'risk assessment processes' to reflect how banks actually assess ML/TF risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners' assessment criteria regarding resource allocation and implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners will assess whether a bank's resource allocation decisions are informed by, and consistent with, reasonably designed risk assessment processes and whether resource-related issues exist that could cause the bank to fail to implement its AML/CFT program in all material respects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While Agencies do not intend examiners to substitute subjective judgment for the bank's reasonable determinations, examiners will evaluate whether the bank knows or should know of implementation/resource issues and whether the bank has addressed them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and conflict-of-interest rules for parties conducting testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual or outside party conducting independent testing must be independent of other parts of the bank's AML/CFT program and oversight; outside parties cannot be government agencies or entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persons who directly or indirectly report to the AML/CFT officer generally would not be sufficiently independent. Outside auditors/consultants engaged must not perform functions that create conflicts of interest (e.g., AML/CFT training or development/enhancement of policies/procedures/controls). Banks with less complex operations may use shared or collaborative arrangements if testing remains independent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program effectiveness expectations and supervisory clarifications sought
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal sets forth conditions for an 'effective' AML/CFT program and solicits comment on whether the description is sufficiently clear or what further clarifications the Agencies should add regarding program effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific comment questions include distinctions between 'establishing' and 'maintaining' programs, defining 'significant or systemic failure' to implement, whether to distinguish establishing/maintaining at program level versus individual-element level, and how to harmonize Agency and FinCEN regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date for final rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agencies propose an effective date of 12 months from issuance of the final rule to allow banks sufficient time to review and implement the proposed requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies solicit comment on the proposed effective date.
